newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.S., UK, Japan futures regulators see closer ties.
newsitem.headline: U.S., UK, Japan futures regulators see closer ties.

text.p: U.S., British and Japanese futures regulators have agreed to cooperate more closely following huge losses Sumitomo Corp. sustained in unauthorised copper deals, official and industry sources said.
An estimated 40 regulators from about 27 countries held a regular meeting in Buergenstock at the start of an annual futures industry conference, the sources said.
The regulators from the three major countries agreed on closer cooperation partly as a result of problems which arose with copper positions held by a single trader.

Sumitomo, one of Japan's giant trading houses, said June 13 that Yasuo Hamanaka lost the money in unauthorised copper trading, mainly on the London Metal Exchange, over a 10-year period. It fired Hamanaka June 14.
The agreement in Buergenstock was in addition to a move towards closer cooperation among the regulators after the collapse of Britain's Barings Bank in late February 1995.
In that case, problems arose due to massive losing positions held in Nikkei index futures contracts listed in Singapore and Osaka, Japan.

"I think they felt that the (initial agreement) was not working as well as it could," said one source who attended Thursday's meeting. He suggested it might have been too broad and involved too many regulators.
Such meetings are usually held without any reporters present, and none of the regulators was immediately available to comment on the record.
